rationale: This is a mechanical symmetry tweak of the archive's SignedNonDepAccrualCashDrain (identical legs, only the short-side gate left un-negated), so it will be near-perfectly correlated with an already-evaluated signal and functions as a diagnostic rather than a new hypothesis.

Smoothing the signed accrual leg over three years and re-gating on accumulated deficits plus liabilities-to-sales is a substantive (persistence vs. one-off shock) change rather than a cosmetic variant, though the base leg is essentially working-capital accruals (Sloan) and the incremental content rests entirely on the distress interaction.

Identical in construction to the archive's ForcedWorkingCapitalLiquidation with only the sales-growth gate swapped for a loss gate, a cosmetic conditioning substitution whose outcome is largely predetermined by the parent.

Crossing the signed opaque-accrual leg with the short-debt/cash-drain gate is a recombination of two archive components rather than a new mechanism, but the pairing is economically coherent, diagnoses whether the earlier weak Fama-MacBeth slope was a gate problem, and is worth one test.

This is effectively WorkingCapitalReliefChurn with gross churn replaced by offsetting churn, and the flipped positive prior is post-hoc rationalization of the earlier sign reversal rather than an independently motivated hypothesis, compounded by extreme construction complexity on ~5% coverage.

The "two independent income-support channels" premise is mechanically false, since ib - oancf + dpc is approximately the negative sum of working-capital changes including -aoloch, so the second leg is a component of the first and the MIN intersection mostly narrows coverage without adding information.
